title: Setting Expectations Early
meta: B2 · 约 280 词 · 场景：明确期望

sections.heading: 1. Surprises Are Usually Late Expectations
paragraphs: At the end of the year, you tell an engineer that he did not show enough ==initiative==.
He looks shocked.
"Nobody ever told me that was part of my job," he says, and he has a point.
Most painful performance conversations are not about bad work.
They are about ==unspoken== expectations that only one side knew about.
You assumed a senior engineer would review other people's designs; he assumed his job was to close his own tickets well.
**If an expectation only lives in your head, it is not an expectation; it is a trap.**
The fix is boring, and it works.
Say what good looks like at the beginning, in plain words, and __write it down__.
It feels ==awkward== to state the obvious, but what is obvious to you is rarely obvious to everyone.
sections.heading_zh: 1. 意外通常是迟到的预期
paragraphs_zh: 年底的时候，你告诉一位工程师，他主动性不够。
他一脸震惊。
「从来没人告诉过我这是我工作的一部分。」他说，而且他说得有道理。
大多数让人难受的绩效谈话，并不是因为活干得差。
而是因为有些预期从没说出口，只有一方知道。
你以为资深工程师会去 review 别人的设计；他以为自己的工作就是把自己的工单做好。
如果一个预期只存在你的脑子里，那它就不是预期，而是陷阱。
解决办法很无聊，但管用。
一开始就用大白话说清楚什么叫做得好，并且写下来。
把显而易见的事说出来会觉得有点别扭，但对你显而易见的东西，很少对每个人都显而易见。

sections.heading: 2. What to Spell Out
paragraphs: Start with outcomes for the first ninety days.
"By the end of March, you own the alerting for the checkout service and have led one postmortem."
Concrete ==milestones== are easier to discuss than adjectives like "strong" or "senior."
Then cover the ==unwritten== rules.
How fast should people reply in chat?
Is it fine to push back on a product manager in a meeting?
These small norms cause more ==friction== than any technical decision.
Be clear about what you will do in return.
"I'll give you feedback within a week of anything important, and I'll tell you early if you're __off track__."
**Expectations work best when they run in both directions.**
Finally, __revisit them__ regularly.
Priorities change, and a list from January can be ==outdated== by June.
A quick check every quarter keeps the agreement alive, and keeps year-end reviews free of surprises.
paragraphs_zh: 从头九十天的结果说起。
「到三月底，你要负责结账服务的告警，并且主导过一次复盘。」
具体的里程碑比「强」或「资深」这种形容词更好讨论。
然后，把那些不成文的规矩讲一讲。
群里消息应该多快回复？
在会上反驳产品经理可以吗？
这些小规矩引起的摩擦，比任何技术决策都多。
也要讲清楚你会怎么回报。
「有任何重要的事，我会在一周内给你反馈；如果你跑偏了，我会尽早告诉你。」
预期是双向的时候，效果最好。
最后，定期回顾。
优先级会变，一月份列的清单到六月可能就过时了。
每个季度快速对一次，能让这份约定一直有效，也能让年底的绩效评估没有意外。

gist.q: 作者认为大多数痛苦的绩效谈话源于什么？
gist.a: 不是工作做得差，而是只有一方知道的、没说出口的期望；只存在你脑子里的期望是陷阱。

gist.q: 一开始应该讲清哪些内容？
gist.a: 前九十天的具体成果和里程碑；不成文的规矩（聊天回复速度、能否在会上反驳 PM）；以及你作为经理会给对方什么。

gist.q: 期望讲清之后还要做什么？
gist.a: 定期回顾，比如每季度检查一次，因为优先级会变，年初的清单到年中可能过时。

prompts.q: 一位资深工程师刚转入你的团队。用 30 秒讲清你对他前三个月的期望，要具体到成果，而不是形容词。
prompts.ref: Let me be concrete about what I'm hoping to see in your first three months. By the end of March, I'd like you to own the alerting for the checkout service, and to have led at least one postmortem. I'd also like you to review designs from the two junior engineers, because that's a big part of the senior role here. In return, I'll give you feedback within a week of anything important.
prompts.ref_zh: 我具体说一下前三个月我希望看到什么。到三月底，我希望你负责结账服务的告警，并且至少主导过一次复盘。我也希望你去 review 那两位初级工程师的设计，因为在我们这儿，这是资深岗位很重要的一部分。作为交换，有任何重要的事，我会在一周内给你反馈。

prompts.q: 团队里经常有人在会上不敢反驳 PM，事后才私下抱怨。用 30 秒在团队会上讲清这条「不成文的规矩」。
prompts.ref: I want to make one expectation explicit, because I don't think I've said it clearly before. If you disagree with a product decision, please say so in the meeting. You won't get in trouble for pushing back, even with senior PMs in the room. What doesn't help is agreeing in the meeting and complaining afterwards, because by then the plan is already moving.
prompts.ref_zh: 有一个预期我想讲明白，因为我觉得之前没说清楚。如果你不同意某个产品决策，请在会上说出来。你反驳不会有任何麻烦，哪怕在座的有资深 PM。没用的是会上同意、会后抱怨，因为到那时方案已经在推进了。

words.ex: She showed initiative by fixing the flaky alert without being asked.
There's an unspoken rule that nobody deploys on Friday.
It's a bit awkward, but we need to talk about the missed deadline.
The first milestone is a working demo by the end of the month.
One unwritten rule here is that you reply to pages within five minutes.
Different code review standards caused friction between the teams.
The runbook is outdated; half the commands no longer work.
Async updates are the norm on our team, not daily meetings.
Tell me early if the project gets off track.
